title: Movable-Type Printing Press
provenance: Public record — fact-checked against historical sources; last verified 2026-10-21.
march_marker: MARCH-TO-A-MILLION: record 1 of 15 archived · target 1,000,000 · in progress
description: Before Gutenberg, every book was copied by hand and cost a fortune. Movable type let one press print thousands of identical pages, collapsing the cost of knowledge and handing it to ordinary people.
what: A press using reusable movable metal type to mass-produce books and texts.
why_revolutionary: It made books cheap and plentiful for the first time, spreading literacy, science, and dissent — the engine of the Reformation and the Scientific Revolution.
evidence: The Gutenberg Bible (c. 1455) survives in about 49 copies; printing spread to more than 200 European cities by 1500.

title: Practical Steam Engine
provenance: Public record — fact-checked against historical sources; last verified 2026-10-21.
march_marker: MARCH-TO-A-MILLION: record 2 of 15 archived · target 1,000,000 · in progress
description: Newcomen's engine wasted heat reheating its cylinder each stroke. Watt's separate condenser made steam power efficient enough to run the factories, trains, and ships that rebuilt the world.
what: A separate-condenser steam engine that turns heat into useful rotary work.
who: James Watt (building on Thomas Newcomen's 1712 engine)
why_revolutionary: It powered the Industrial Revolution — pumping mines, driving mills, and later locomotives and ships — multiplying human productivity beyond muscle and water.
evidence: Watt's 1769 patent and the Boulton & Watt partnership; hundreds of engines working across Britain by 1800.

title: Vaccination
provenance: Public record — fact-checked against historical sources; last verified 2026-10-21.
march_marker: MARCH-TO-A-MILLION: record 3 of 15 archived · target 1,000,000 · in progress
description: Jenner noticed milkmaids who caught cowpox never caught smallpox. His 1796 test on a boy, then published evidence, founded immunology and has since saved billions of lives.
what: Deliberate mild exposure (cowpox) to confer immunity against smallpox.
why_revolutionary: The first scientific immunization — the ancestor of every vaccine — proving the immune system could be trained safely.
evidence: Jenner's 1798 'Inquiry'; global vaccination eradicated smallpox, declared gone in 1980 — the only human disease ever eradicated.

title: Surgical Anesthesia
provenance: Public record — fact-checked against historical sources; last verified 2026-10-21.
march_marker: MARCH-TO-A-MILLION: record 4 of 15 archived · target 1,000,000 · in progress
description: Surgeons once raced the clock while patients screamed. Morton's public ether demonstration proved pain could simply be switched off, and within years no reputable surgeon operated without it.
what: Ether anesthesia making painless surgery possible.
who: William T. G. Morton (public demonstration, Massachusetts General Hospital)
why_revolutionary: It turned surgery from a desperate, agonizing last resort into a careful science — without it, modern surgery cannot exist.
evidence: The 1846-10-16 Ether Dome demonstration; anesthesia spread to operating rooms worldwide within a few years.

title: Evolution by Natural Selection

description: Darwin showed that nature itself does the selecting: organisms best suited to their world leave more offspring. DNA later confirmed the mechanism he could only infer.
what: The theory that species change over generations through natural selection.
why_revolutionary: It unified all of biology under one explanatory framework — every living thing connected by descent.
evidence: 'On the Origin of Species' (1859); confirmed by genetics, the fossil record, and directly observed evolution.

title: Practical Incandescent Light
provenance: Public record — fact-checked against historical sources; last verified 2026-10-21.

why_revolutionary: It brought affordable electric light into homes and cities, extending the productive day and transforming urban life.
evidence: Edison's 1879 Menlo Park lamp burned 13+ hours; his Pearl Street station lit lower Manhattan in 1882.

title: Penicillin
provenance: Public record — fact-checked against historical sources; last verified 2026-10-21.
march_marker: MARCH-TO-A-MILLION: record 9 of 15 archived · target 1,000,000 · in progress
description: Fleming noticed mold killing bacteria in a petri dish. A decade later Florey and Chain turned the curiosity into a drug — and infections stopped being death sentences.

description: Vacuum tubes were hot, fragile, and huge. The transistor did the same job in a sliver of crystal — and made the entire digital age physically possible.

title: DNA Double Helix
provenance: Public record — fact-checked against historical sources; last verified 2026-10-21.
march_marker: MARCH-TO-A-MILLION: record 11 of 15 archived · target 1,000,000 · in progress
description: The structure suggested the copying mechanism immediately: unzip the helix, build two from one. It turned heredity from mystery into readable information.

why_revolutionary: It founded molecular biology — reading and writing the code of life, from genetics to gene therapy.
